item.title: FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election
item.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of member associations in his bid for re-election despite criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) rallied behind Infantino on Friday in a significant boost to the 56-year-old’s hopes of winning a fourth term in charge. Infantino’s future in the role was in doubt two months ago when he faced a furious backlash to his plan to sell off a portion of the commercial rights of competitions run by football’s world governing body to private investors. The heads of European football’s governing body UEFA, the AFC and CONCACAF, which runs the game in North and Central America, signed a letter saying football “belongs to no individual”. But Infantino, who apologised last week for the failed private investment project, is now in a strong position to secure re-election in March. “I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view,” Infantino told the BBC on Saturday. “But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority. “I’m just coming back off Tokyo where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde where all African countries have endorsed me. I’m speaking to all associations everywhere in the world.” No other candidate has yet come forward to oppose Infantino with the deadline to do so less than a month away on November 18. He added: “There are different points of view it’s not always easy to bring them all under one roof but we need to respect and I do respect all opinions all views and then it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run.” The post FIFA: Infantino says backed by ‘vast majority’ in bid for re-election appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alake’s attack on Atiku won’t cut food prices, ADC campaign fires back
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has fired back at Information Minister Dele Alake over his allegations against former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, saying no amount of political propaganda can shield President Bola Tinubu’s administration from public anger over rising living costs. The council argued that Nigerians were more concerned about the cost of food, fuel and transportation than allegations of artificial intelligence manipulation and deepfakes, challenging Alake to produce evidence linking Atiku or the ADC to the alleged fabricated letter and video. In a statement on Saturday, Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, described Alake’s intervention as an attempt to divert attention from the government’s record, insisting that the economic hardship confronting Nigerians was real and undeniable. “Until then, his ‘fake news alert’ is an empty political stunt,” Shaibu said, challenging the minister to provide names, dates and forensic findings to substantiate his allegations. Citing petrol prices of about ₦1,400 per litre, diesel prices above ₦2,000 and food inflation hovering around 20 per cent, Shaibu said the economic pressures facing households could not be dismissed as fabricated information. The council also cited a World Bank poverty estimate reported by Reuters, arguing that the administration’s economic direction had left millions of Nigerians struggling to make ends meet. Many retailers in the capital had wooden boards covering windows. A heavy police presence could be seen in Place de la Bastille, along with many journalists, but few protesters. Police used a megaphone to tell the crowd that the demonstration had been banned from the area, telling protesters to go to the alternate route near Porte d’Italie “immediately”. Earlier, a police helicopter could be seen flying over the city, with security forces patrolling and armoured vehicles and riot police vans parked nearby. Calls to defy the bans on protests in the city centre had circulated on social media. ‘Improvise’ Shopkeepers in boarded-up Paris said they were unsure what to expect. “It feels like we’re all just going to have to improvise a bit… We’ve secured everything as best we can, we’ll likely close at 1:00 pm and then stay in the vicinity to keep an eye on things,” Armelle Gueganton, a bookseller in the 12th arrondissement, told AFP. She worried about the route that authorities had mandated for the main Paris rally, pointing out that parts of it were “extremely narrow” and that it passed by a petrol station. “I have to wonder if they even have Google Maps at the prefecture when they authorise routes like this.” ‘Break Things’ Shops were also boarded up in the southwestern city of Bordeaux. “Boarding up five storefronts like ours … costs us nearly 5,000 euros ($5,600),” Margaux Rey, manager of the Altermundi shop, told AFPTV. “There is a high demand for securing shops ahead of the upcoming demonstrations,” confirmed Joseph Fernandez, a tradesman who was “scrambling” to meet the requests — though, he added, if individuals “want to break things, they will”. A protester speaks in a microphone as others hold a banner reading “neither congress nor meeting for the RN” during a demonstration “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the Congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France on October 24, 2026. On Patrol Numerous riot police vans could be seen in Marseille, along with armoured vehicles and water cannon. Philippe Mamelli, 64, said he was “patrolling” the southern port city’s thoroughfares armed with a truncheon at his waist and pepper spray in his pocket before heading to a demonstration later. He said he was part of a group called “Citizen Revolution” which sought to support the student protesters, adding: “The rioters are undermining” the student demands. item.title: 2027: Jigawa APC unveils campaign structure, names Namadi chairman
item.description: ‎ By Muhammad Inuwa ,Dutse ‎ The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Jigawa State has unveiled its campaign structure for the 2027 general elections, appointing Governor Umar Namadi as chairman and former governors Ali Sa’adu Birnin Kudu and Ibrahim Saminu Turaki as deputy chairmen. ‎ The structure is designed to coordinate campaign activities, strengthen party structures and mobilise grassroots support across the state’s 27 local government areas ahead of the elections. ‎ The appointments were announced in a statement dated October 22, 2026, and signed by the state APC chairman, Hon. Ahmed Garba. ‎ According to the statement, the party’s State Working Committee approved the composition of the campaign council following consultations with party leaders and stakeholders across the state. ‎ The council has six vice chairmen representing the three senatorial districts, with two representatives from each zone to ensure broad participation and effective coordination of campaign activities. ‎ For Jigawa North-East, Senator Muhammad Ibrahim and Senator Ibrahim Hassan Hadejia were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II, respectively. ‎ In Jigawa South-West, the Speaker of the Jigawa State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, and Hon. Farouk Adamu Aliyu were named Vice Chairmen I and II. ‎ Similarly, Alhaji Jisa Gerawa and Hajiya Rabi Ishaq were appointed Vice Chairmen I and II for Jigawa North-West Senatorial District. ‎ The party also named Alhaji Lawan Yau Roni as director-general of the campaign council, responsible for coordinating its day-to-day activities and implementing campaign programmes. ‎ The council is expected to provide strategic direction, coordinate campaign operations and strengthen engagement with party leaders, members and supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ Garba urged members of the council, party leaders and supporters to demonstrate unity, discipline, loyalty and commitment to the party’s electoral objectives. ‎ He reaffirmed the APC’s commitment to progressive governance, democratic development and advancing the interests of the people of Jigawa State, while calling on members to work together towards the party’s success in the forthcoming elections. item.title: Jigawa govt denies giving houses to Kannywood actors
item.description: ‎ ‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎Jigawa State Government has dismissed allegations that it allocated houses in the Danmodi Housing Estate in Ringim to popular APC musician Dauda Kahutu Rarara and members of the Triple R group. ‎ ‎Dady Ringim, a new media aide to Governor Umar Namadi, described the allegation as false and lacking factual basis while reacting to the controversy on social media. ‎ ‎The controversy followed a viral video in which Rarara and members of Triple R allegedly claimed that the governor had allocated houses to them”. The video has triggered reactions from opposition figures and other social media users in the state. ‎Among those who criticised the alleged allocation was Zakari Kafin Hausa, a former aide to Governor Namadi and a prominent critic of his administration and ADC Candidate for Auyo/Kafin Hausa House of Representatives in the 2027 election. ‎ ‎In his Facebook post, Kafin Hausa questioned the reported allocation of the houses, particularly as the housing project was allegedly financed with public funds. ‎ ‎ “There are certain decisions taken by this administration that I am wondering whether it is the Umar Namadi we have always known making them or he has been replaced with ‘Jibrin from Sudan.’” ‎ ‎He also questioned why public housing projects should be allocated in such a manner. ‎ ‎However, reacting to the criticism, Ringim accused Kafin Hausa of overlooking the governor’s achievements, arguing that Namadi’s projects and policies were strengthening his popularity and re-election prospects. According to him, “The Triple R statement does not mean the Governor has gift them Houses, they are trying to establish the fact that the Governor has constructed the affordable Housing Estate for the People of the state. “The Danmodi Housing Estate was constructed across the whole 27 Local Government of the state and are available for the citizens whoever meet the requirements” he said. “What they are doing are doing it to advertise the good work of Governor Umar Namadi, not only Housing Estate including Tsangaya, Roads, Health, Agriculture among other.” ‎He said the governor’s achievements were making a lasting impression on the people, adding that “politics is not built on rhetoric alone; it requires action and the trust of the people.” ‎ ‎Ringim expressed confidence that voters would determine the state’s political future, insisting that the administration’s performance was helping to build a lasting legacy, particularly among young people. ‎ ‎He urged political actors to verify information before making public allegations, warning that political differences should not be allowed to encourage the spread of misinformation. ‎ ‎The controversy has generated debate on social media over the alleged allocation of the houses and the management of publicly funded housing projects in Jigawa State. item.title: 10 killed as armed bandits raid Taraba community, loot food stores
item.description: By Femi Bolaji, Jalingo No fewer than ten residents were reportedly gunned down on Friday afternoon when a large gang of heavily armed bandits invaded Binnari village in Taraba State, unleashing intense gunfire and looting food supplies from shops. According to a police statement issued by the Taraba State Police Command Public Relations Officer, ASP Victor Mshelizah, the tragic attack occurred on Friday, October 23, 2026, at about 3:00 p.m., shortly after residents concluded Jumu’ah prayers. The assailants, numbering in their dozens, threw the rural community into pandemonium as they shot indiscriminately before pillaging food items and provision stores. Operatives attached to the Binnari police station, upon receiving distress calls, mobilised to the scene alongside community volunteers, recovering ten corpses bearing fatal gunshot wounds. The victims have since been handed over to their respective families and buried in accordance with Islamic rites. Reacting to the carnage, the State Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, placed security formations across the area on red alert and ordered the immediate deployment of joint tactical teams comprising the Nigeria Police Force, Police Mobile Force (PMF), and the Nigerian Army to comb the surrounding terrain. The command urged residents of Binnari and neighbouring settlements to remain calm, avoid panic peddling, and cooperate with security operatives by sharing actionable intelligence that will lead to the apprehension of the fleeing attackers. item.title: Kaduna Presidential Rally: Atiku is butterfly thinking itself a bird – Keyamo
item.description: Festus Keyamo, Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, has described Atiku Abubakar as a butterfly that thinks it is a bird, given his “blistering online attack against the APC (All Progressives Congress), particularly in the North”. The APC is scheduled to flag off its presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. According to Keyamo, Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress, ADC, was banking on the bulk of Northern votes to see him through in 2027, knowing that he has no inroads at all into the South. Therefore, Keyamo said in a statement, Atiku has taken to the “common but cheap tactic” of positioning cameras then get people to tear down the posters of President Bola Tinubu, and then post the videos online. “The other tactic is to disseminate disinformation claiming that any support the President is seen to receive in the North is procured only through the massive deployment of financial resources. “Hence the fake letter alleging a N2.3 trillion deployment for the Kaduna rally. item.title: Chelsea vs Tottenham: Preview, team news, possible line-ups
item.description: Chelsea will look to extend their winning run in the Premier League when they host Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday in a London derby that could have significant implications for both sides. Chelsea have won four, drawn one and lost two of their opening seven league matches, leaving them in the top four. Their recent results have also boosted confidence, with a 5-1 victory over Bournemouth followed by a 2-0 win away to Everton last weekend. Pedro Neto scored twice against Everton as Chelsea ended a run of 22 Premier League matches without a clean sheet. The Blues will now attempt to record three consecutive league victories for the first time since February. The West London club have won their last six league meetings with Tottenham. Another victory on Saturday would set a new club record for consecutive league wins against their London rivals. Tottenham, meanwhile, ended a six-game winless start to the league campaign with a 3-1 victory over Coventry. James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies scored to give Roberto De Zerbi’s side a much-needed result. The win was Tottenham’s fourth Premier League victory in 2026 and the first time in 36 top-flight matches that they had scored more than twice. Despite the result, Spurs remain 16th in the table, although they are only three points behind the top nine. They will need to improve their away record against Chelsea to secure another positive result. Tottenham have won only once in their last 34 Premier League visits to Stamford Bridge, recording 11 draws and 24 defeats. Their most recent victory there came in the 2017-18 season, when Mauricio Pochettino guided them to a 3-1 win. Spurs have also lost their last six London derbies in the league and will be keen to avoid extending that run. Team news Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is set to miss the match after undergoing surgery for a fractured jaw sustained during the win over Everton. He joins Reece James, Jamie Gittens, Pep Chavarria and Emmanuel Emegha on the injury list. Malo Gusto, however, is available again after recovering from illness. Mike Penders is expected to start in goal in Martinez’s absence. The 21-year-old could become Chelsea’s youngest goalkeeper to start a Premier League match. For Tottenham, Rodrigo Bentancur remains suspended and will serve the second match of his three-game ban. Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall and Destiny Udogie are also sidelined with knee injuries, while Savio is unavailable because of a muscle problem. Mykhaylo Mudryk, who is on loan from Chelsea, is ineligible to face his parent club and is also recovering from an ankle injury. Tosin Adarabioyo is a doubt with a calf problem, but Pedro Porro, Omar Marmoush and Andrew Robertson have been passed fit to play. item.title: Keyamo accuses Atiku of fearing APC’s Northern support
item.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of being apprehensive about the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s support base in northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Keyamo, a senior advocate of Nigeria, made the allegation in a statement titled, “Why Atiku Abubakar Is Particularly Jittery About the Kaduna Flag-off,” in which he criticised the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate’s reported online attacks against the APC ahead of the party’s campaign rally in Kaduna State. He alleged that some videos circulating online showing the removal of President Bola Tinubu’s campaign posters were staged to create the impression that the President had lost support in the North. Keyamo also dismissed as fake a purported letter alleging that N2.3 trillion had been earmarked for the Kaduna rally, describing it as an attempt to portray the APC as relying on financial inducements to attract supporters. The minister, however, did not provide evidence in the statement to substantiate his allegations about the videos or the purported letter. He argued that Atiku’s political calculations ahead of the 2027 election had been based largely on securing northern votes, adding that the former vice-president faced challenges in gaining support in the South. Keyamo cited the 2023 presidential election, claiming that Atiku lost across the North-Central states and all Southern states except Osun State. He alleged that Atiku had initially expected Tinubu to have limited electoral appeal in the North but was now concerned about the APC’s political structures in the region. According to Keyamo, the APC’s presence in northern Nigeria could undermine Atiku’s strategy of relying on the region to secure victory in the next presidential election. The minister further argued that even a strong showing by Atiku in parts of the North might not be sufficient to secure victory if he failed to make significant gains in the Middle Belt and Southern states. Keyamo also drew a comparison between Atiku and former President Muhammadu Buhari, who secured substantial northern support in the 2015 presidential election. He argued that Atiku’s political background differed from Buhari’s, while making corruption-related allegations against the former vice-president without presenting supporting evidence in the statement. The comments come amid intensifying political activity ahead of the 2027 general elections, with parties and their presidential contenders seeking to consolidate support across the country’s geopolitical zones. item.title: Police fire tear gas as new French demonstrations kick off
item.description: French police started firing tear gas at protesters Saturday as they stepped up security in major cities aiming to prevent a repeat of rioting a week ago, on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the high cost of living. Police in the southeast city of Lyon fired tear gas to disperse some 150 protesters near the city centre — where demonstrations had been banned — when they briefly tried to block a road, an AFP journalist saw. Elsewhere, authorities and rattled shopkeepers geared up for potential new street violence. Near Paris’s Bastille neighbourhood, a clothing store had removed all its merchandise from shelves ahead of the demonstrations, while a nearby restaurant was boarded up with signs insisting it was “still open”. Many other retailers in the capital also had wooden boards covering their windows. The Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums were closed. Police were seen readying riot gear in zones that bore the brunt of last weekend’s clashes and looting. They were among 70,000 security personnel the interior ministry said were mobilised to counter the “high” threat of violence. “We will not tolerate any unrest,” Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday, adding that calls had been circulating on social media calling for violence and looting. – Protest against far-right party – Adding to tensions, far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party was holding a weekend congress in the central city of Orleans to kick off her campaign for elections in six months to choose President Emmanuel Macron’s successor. Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched on Saturday against Le Pen, and also against Macron, a pro-business centrist leader. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled. The violence last weekend and the heightened tensions over this weekend’s demonstrations highlighted the febrile atmosphere in France ahead of that vote, which Le Pen is best-placed, according to surveys, to win. item.title: 2027: Arewa‘ll return Tinubu to Aso Rock – Musa Kwankwaso
item.description: A member of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Musa Kwankwaso, says the North-West will return President Bola Tinubu to Aso Rock by voting for him massively in the 2027 general elections. Kwankwaso spoke against the backdrop of the massive turnout and endorsement of Tinubu at the formal kick-off of the APC Presidential Campaign on Saturday in Kaduna. Kwankwaso described the gathering as a decisive demonstration of Northern support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 polls. The APC campaign council member said the Kaduna rally had effectively dispelled lingering doubts over where the North stood in the unfolding presidential contest. “Today, we of the North-West geopolitical zone have spoken loud and clear on who we stand for. Our choice of Tinubu remains our commitment to a better Nigeria and national cohesion,” he said. Kwankwaso said that the significance of the Kaduna gathering extended beyond the immediate political mobilisation. He argued that the North had sent a strong message to other geopolitical zones on the need to consolidate around Tinubu for the sake of national progress. According to him, the president’s administration represents an opportunity to deepen equitable development and ensure that the country’s resources are distributed fairly across the six geopolitical zones. “Tinubu’s presidency stands for fair and equitable distribution of resources to all zones, and his return will be a blessing to the greater Nigeria of our dream.” He also dismissed any suggestion that the North’s support for Tinubu was merely transactional, saying the region had a responsibility to honour its political commitment and remain united behind the President as the 2027 election approaches. “Asiwaju is the northern candidate, and he will not promote anything outside his ambition because we are trustworthy people, and we shall deliver him come 2027,” he said. He urged Nigerians, particularly political stakeholders across the geopolitical zones to view the emerging support for Tinubu through the prism of national unity and collective progress, rather than narrow political interests. He emphasised that the Kaduna mobilisation had demonstrated that the North had already made its choice. The government described the purported letter as fraudulent and misleading, accusing its authors of attempting to damage the governor’s reputation for fiscal discipline and responsible governance. The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki, stated this in a statement on Saturday in Kaduna. He said the purported letter, allegedly addressed to Sen. item.title: Campaign Turns Ugly As Israeli Election Nears
item.description: Days ahead of close-fought Israeli elections, campaigns have gone into overdrive with poor-taste jibes and inflammatory attacks against candidates, sometimes crossing red lines. Fuelled in part by a boom in AI-generated images flooding social media, candidates and activists are seeking to portray their opponents as weak, untrustworthy or damaging for the country as they play on stereotypes and fears to sway public opinion. The electioneering has at times turned personal, with some candidates who lost loved ones in the wars following Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack even having their bereavement dragged into the campaign. Ahead of Tuesday’s vote, polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc neck and neck with that of his main centre-right rival Gadi Eisenkot. On Wednesday, Eisenkot posted a video on X wishing Netanyahu a happy 77th birthday that featured a slate of AI-generated characters including a Hamas member speaking from a tunnel. “What can we wish for the person who has been protecting us for 20 years?” the militant says, evoking theories that the premier has deliberately helped the Islamist movement stay in power in Gaza, charges vehemently denied by Netanyahu. Soon after, an AI depiction of Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei pops up, telling Netanyahu: “One more round without victory and I’ll make you a bomb as a present.” Netanyahu has also liberally weaponised AI-generated content against his rival. item.title: It’s unfair to compare us to Barca – Real Madrid’s Mourinho
item.description: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said it was unfair to compare his side to Spanish champions Barcelona ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico. Hansi Flick’s Barca have won back-to-back La Liga titles and lead the top flight, in which they are unbeaten, while Mourinho arrived this summer after Madrid went two seasons without a major trophy. The panorama has changed slightly, after Barca suffered their first defeat of the season at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday, while Madrid have won their last four matches. Madrid are third in La Liga, trailing Barca by six points before Sunday’s meeting at Camp Nou. “I think the people that thought a week ago Barca would thrash us will keep thinking the same thing,” Mourinho told reporters on Saturday. “I don’t think just for the Paris game, or Madrid’s (4-1 win against) Leipzig, they will change their way of thinking.” Mourinho highlighted that he has only been at the helm a few months, in comparison to Flick, who arrived at Barca in 2024. “People look at us like a finished product, but finished products in football are difficult because they are never finished… but they look at us like we’re in an advanced phase of the process,” continued Mourinho. “We’ve been working for three months, out of that you can take pre-season when the players were arriving (back from the World Cup), and the recent international break, then we’ve been together a month-and-a-half, two months… “This is the start of a product, we’re in an initial phase where the coach is learning, analysing, bit by bit defining paths, the players are learning about the coach… comparing a team in this state (to more established sides), I think is unfair.” Mourinho said form did not matter when it comes to the Clasico. “We’ve been in a good dynamic, winning games, playing well, scoring goals, but in the Clasico it doesn’t matter what you did before, it has no influence,” said Mourinho. “The Clasico is unique, normally the football world stops to watch it. Hopefully it’s a great game. And we win.” Mourinho said he would not change his plans to try and stop Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old Spain international is in sublime form and hopes to win the Ballon d’Or award on Monday. “He’s a great player and great players you respect,” added Mourinho. “One thing is respecting, another thing is to change plans, structures, forgetting your own essence. That we will not do, neither for him or any other player of great quality we face.” AFP The post It’s unfair to compare us to Barca – Real Madrid’s Mourinho appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Edo Govt, NLC Resolve Dispute As NUEE Moves To Restore Electricity
item.description: Electricity supply is set to be restored in Edo State after Governor Monday Okpebholo and leaders of organised labour settled the dispute over recognition of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) caretaker committee in the state. According to a Press Release by the Chief Press Secretary to the governor, Patrick Ebojele, the agreement was reached at a closed-door meeting in Abuja convened by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume. Also present were NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero; Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi; and former Edo State Governor and ex-NLC President, Senator Adams Oshiomhole. Speaking to journalists after the meeting, Governor Okpebholo said the parties had resolved the matter. According to him, the state government would recognise the caretaker committee and work with labour leaders on arrangements for a substantive election. “There is no issue actually, and we have resolved the issues that border the NLC caretaker committee in Edo,” he said. The Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo, the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, Minister of Labour and Employment, Dr Muhammad Maigari Dingyadi, former Edo State Governor and ex-NLC President, Senator Adams Oshiomhole and others at the settlement meeting in Abuja. Ajaero confirmed the agreement and thanked the Governor, Akume, Dingyadi and Oshiomhole for their roles. He said labour had agreed to work with the state government on recognising the caretaker committee, organising a substantive election, and addressing the rights and privileges due to the committee. “Consequently, power will be restored in Edo,” Ajaero said. Oshiomhole described the dispute as a communication gap, which he said had now been resolved. He said the reason for continuing the action no longer existed. He also noted the Governor’s offer to rebuild trust between the Edo State Government and organised labour, and said renewed cooperation was needed to maintain industrial harmony. Dingyadi said the parties had agreed to work together for the peace and progress of Edo State and Nigeria. He said the NLC would conduct a substantive election in Edo within three to six months. “The principal issue, which is electricity, is going to be restored immediately,” the minister said. Akume commended the participants for their willingness to settle the matter through dialogue. The power outage followed two related but separate disputes. The first was an industrial disagreement between BEDC Electricity Plc and the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE) over workers’ pay and welfare. The second was a leadership dispute with the Edo State NLC, led by Joseph Igbafe, over recognition of its caretaker committee. item.title: ‘I want to leave Aso Rock in 2031 to a Nigeria I can enjoy’ — Remi Tinubu
item.description: Nigeria’s First Lady, Remi Tinubu, says she hopes to leave the Presidential Villa in 2031 to a country she can enjoy as a woman in her 70s. She spoke on Friday while inaugurating the Abuja headquarters of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, a grassroots group mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. “I want to leave Aso Rock, in 2031, by the grace of God, and enter a Nigeria that me as a 70-something-year-old woman will enjoy,” she said. “I want to get to the airport. I want to travel, you know, so quickly. And you can see our airports too are changing,” she said. She added that some Nigerians might not recognise the changes taking place, joking that they could be given “Bola Tinubu eyeglasses”. “So things are happening in Nigeria, except, you know, those who don’t see; maybe we’ll give them some, you know, Bola Tinubu eyeglasses. We are doing that, JigiBola,” she said. Remi Tinubu later formally commissioned the movement’s Abuja headquarters and expressed support for her husband’s bid for a second term. “So to the glory of God, and for the victory of Mr President come 2027, I hereby formally commission the PBAT door-to-door movement campaign headquarters Abuja,” she said. item.title: ‘Weeks, not days’ in Kompany recovery, say Bayern
item.description: Bayern Munich expect coach Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as he continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern sporting director Max Eberl confirmed Kompany was still hospitalised in a “stable” condition. Kompany’s English assistant coach Aaron Danks will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl told reporters “examinations were continuing” to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined. “Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We’re not starting to put together any timeframes. “We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we’ll discuss calmly what recovery time is to be. We won’t be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that.” Taking Saturday’s press conference in Kompany’s absence, Danks said he had spoken with the former centre-back briefly on Friday but only to wish him well. “I explained to him that we wouldn’t be having no football conversations. It was just checking in on his health and making sure he’s OK. “All the football operations are in our hands and we’ll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward.” Bayern’s second team’s game was postponed yesterday after Kompany’s collapse but Eberl said the club did not consider trying to postpone Sunday’s Bundesliga game. “I think the greatest joy for Vinnie would be for us to play well tomorrow and, ideally, get a positive result,” Eberl said. “That would probably be one of the best things we could do to help him recover.” Danks confirmed Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, who has been on bereavement leave since Tuesday, would also miss Sunday’s game. Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday’s home clash with Arsenal despite missing the pre-match press conference due to the virus. Speaking after the Arsenal game, Kompany said his body reacted after he tried to push through the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body — and then at some point my body just said, ‘enough is enough!'” The defending champions sit on top of the Bundesliga table ahead of Sunday’s game, one point above Freiburg. Kompany’s English assistant coach Aaron Danks will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl told reporters “examinations were continuing” to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined. “Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We’re not starting to put together any timeframes. “We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we’ll discuss calmly what recovery time is to be. We won’t be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that.” Taking Saturday’s press conference in Kompany’s absence, Danks said he had spoken with the former centre-back briefly on Friday but only to wish him well. “I explained to him that we wouldn’t be having no football conversations. It was just checking in on his health and making sure he’s OK. “All the football operations are in our hands and we’ll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward.” Bayern’s second team’s game was postponed yesterday after Kompany’s collapse but Eberl said the club did not consider trying to postpone Sunday’s Bundesliga game. “I think the greatest joy for Vinnie would be for us to play well tomorrow and, ideally, get a positive result,” Eberl said. “That would probably be one of the best things we could do to help him recover.” Danks confirmed Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, who has been on bereavement leave since Tuesday, would also miss Sunday’s game. Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday’s home clash with Arsenal despite missing the pre-match press conference due to the virus. Speaking after the Arsenal game, Kompany said his body reacted after he tried to push through the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body — and then at some point my body just said, ‘enough is enough!'” The defending champions sit on top of the Bundesliga table ahead of Sunday’s game, one point above Freiburg. item.title: North Korea’s Kim calls for training world’s ‘strongest’ military
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un urged his military to train to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media said Saturday. Kim’s call for what he dubbed a “Korean-style military revolution” came the same week Seoul’s military proposed talks to clarify the border after an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) further strained inter-Korean ties. Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war as the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce, not a peace treaty. The Pyongyang event, held Thursday and Friday, was aimed at developing a plan “to train the strongest armed forces in the world,” Kim said, according to the official Korea Central News Agency (KCNA). He also called for “all the companies” of the North’s army to be “turned into a strong elite unit in military and technical aspects and consolidated into perfect combat forces”. KCNA said it was the first gathering of “the entire army” since a February party congress where Kim had called for stronger conventional forces and reaffirmed plans to develop nuclear weapons and missiles. North Korea has also tested a slew of weapons recently, including a “new-type” precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile, both of which were said to use AI technology. Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible. The North has also become a key Russian ally since it launched its invasion of Ukraine in 2022, sending troops to support Moscow’s war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology. South Korea proposed on Friday military talks with North Korea to clarify their border and restore communication channels, after Seoul blamed the DMZ blast that injured South Korean soldiers on North Korean landmines, a claim Pyongyang strongly rejected. Pyongyang, which also previously rejected Seoul’s demand for an apology over the explosion, has not responded to Friday’s proposal. c The post North Korea’s Kim calls for training world’s ‘strongest’ military appeared first on Vanguard News .

Uduaghan was at the church to thank God for His mercies all these years. People turned out in numbers in the church where the pastor preached about the Holy Spirit. The word of God was good. And the people reveled in it. As the service was about to end, the pastor invited Uduaghan to make a brief remark after the church had prayed for him and his family. When he was done, the pastor prayed that more good things would continue to follow him. Uduaghan recalled one moment, as Governor of Delta State when he was caught between life and death and God saved his life. Part of his testimony went thus: “There are two things associated with governance. I call them the two Ps. They are Power and Pain. You see a governor and you marvel at the power he commands. He can order the arrest of somebody, he moves in a convoy, he has so much power that he earns tremendous respect everywhere. People see the glamour and the glitz, etc. But they don’t see the pain. There’s pain in governance. You can only rely on the grace of God to guide and guard you. ”When I came in as governor in 2007, the violence we battled then in Delta was more than what is happening now with the Avengers, etc. Kidnapping was high and expatriates were leaving. Militancy was more than what we have now. President Yar’Adua called me and said ‘what’s going on? These things are happening in your state.’ I told him that there were kaytwo ways to handle the militancy in Niger Delta. I asked that the Federal Government should do their own and I would do my own. We set out to work. I had to go to the creeks. We had to dialogue with these people. ”I remember one Sunday, my family and I had prepared to go to church and I received a call that they were going to burn Chevron terminal. The facility they planned to burn was so huge the impact would have been terrible for our oil production. I told them I would come after church service but they insisted I should come immediately otherwise the militants would destroy the terminal. I had to leave. I told my family to pray for me at the church. It was just one of my trips to the creeks. I took helicopter and then did the final journey by boat. And you know that when you go on such trips to the creeks you don’t take escorts or when you take them they don’t carry guns. I went with only my ADC. No guns. It was a huge risk but one that I had to take to engage them and stop the blowing up of the oil facilities. ”It was a terrible place. I continued the journey further into the creeks to meet their superiors. I got there and they led me into a room. They were kind enough to offer me a seat. It was a moment of life or death within seconds. You could see the anger on the face of the militant, who pointed the gun at me. He wanted to shoot. It was terrifying. There was nothing I could do but to pray silently. I was praying. Silently, I prayed and I waved the white handkerchief (peace signal) I had. The man steadied the gun at me. item.title: The Road To 2027 Runs Through Kaduna, But The North Is Not A Number
item.description: President Bola Tinubu will formally open his re-election campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. The location is deliberate, the arithmetic is formidable, and the message is unmistakable: the All Progressives Congress intends to win the 2027 election by rebuilding a northern coalition around the President. The three northern geopolitical zones contain 56.01 million of Nigeria’s 103.43 million registered voters; 54.2 per cent of the national register. The North-West alone has 25.08 million, making it the country’s largest electoral bloc. APC campaign officials are consequently talking about northern consensus and setting a national target of approximately 40 million votes. But registered voters are not actual votes, political endorsements are not public opinion, and the North is not a single electoral personality. That is the political signal this week. Why Kaduna matters Kaduna is in the North-West region. Kaduna is an appropriate starting point because it captures both the opportunity and the danger confronting Tinubu. It is a major political centre in the North-West, but it is not naturally secure territory for the President. Tinubu lost Kaduna to Atiku Abubakar in 2023. item.content:encoded: President Bola Tinubu will formally open his re-election campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. The location is deliberate, the arithmetic is formidable, and the message is unmistakable: the All Progressives Congress intends to win the 2027 election by rebuilding a northern coalition around the President. The three northern geopolitical zones contain 56.01 million of Nigeria’s 103.43 million registered voters; 54.2 per cent of the national register. The North-West alone has 25.08 million, making it the country’s largest electoral bloc. APC campaign officials are consequently talking about northern consensus and setting a national target of approximately 40 million votes. But registered voters are not actual votes, political endorsements are not public opinion, and the North is not a single electoral personality. That is the political signal this week. Why Kaduna matters Kaduna is in the North-West region. Kaduna is an appropriate starting point because it captures both the opportunity and the danger confronting Tinubu. It is a major political centre in the North-West, but it is not naturally secure territory for the President. Tinubu lost Kaduna to Atiku Abubakar in 2023. The state also embodies several issues that could determine northern voting behaviour: insecurity, rural poverty, food prices, religious sensitivity and the relationship between elite political agreements and popular sentiment. By beginning there, the APC is signalling that it will not concede the region to Atiku merely because he is a northern Muslim. It is relying on Vice-President Kashim Shettima, governors, ministers, traditional relationships and a greatly expanded party structure to offset Atiku’s regional appeal. That structure matters. The APC now enjoys an extraordinary advantage in the number of governors, lawmakers and local political networks under its control. Governors influence campaign financing, mobilisation and the organisation required to convert public sympathy into votes. The party’s challenge is that political machinery can mobilise supporters, but it cannot permanently insulate an incumbent from lived economic experience. The contest between structure and hardship The APC’s campaign argument will be that the most painful period of reform has passed. Inflation has moderated, foreign reserves have improved, economic growth has strengthened, and the Central Bank has begun adjusting interest rates. The administration will argue that removing the petrol subsidy and reforming the foreign-exchange market prevented a deeper fiscal crisis. The opposition’s reply is more immediate: food, transport, energy and business costs remain painfully high. That explains the political significance of the National Economic Council’s newly approved 90-day action plan. It prioritises food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, removal of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. It also proposes a national dashboard to track projects and the use of savings from subsidy removal. On paper, these are reasonable interventions. The problem is timing. The presidential election is 86 days away, while the relief plan is designed to run for 90 days. Atiku’s campaign has therefore called it “election bait,” arguing that Nigerians are being asked to vote before the promised relief can be fully assessed. That is a partisan allegation, not proof that the programme is improper. But the calendar gives the criticism political force. The government can answer it only through early, measurable delivery. What food has become cheaper? Which households have received support? What projects have been completed? How much has been spent, by whom and under what criteria? Announcements will not be sufficient. The electorate needs receipts. The opposition’s unity problem While the APC prepares a major campaign launch, opposition parties are again discussing a consensus candidate. Representatives of the ADC, NDC, PRP, SDP, APM and PDP have inaugurated legal and media committees to develop a framework for cooperation. Atiku, Peter Obi, Donald Duke and Adewale Adebayo are among the names mentioned in the talks. Coalition organisers say negotiations are progressing towards a single candidate. That claim should be treated cautiously. The Independent National Electoral Commission has already published 18 presidential candidates, including Atiku for the ADC and Obi for the NDC. Agreeing that the opposition should unite is therefore much easier than determining who withdraws, who leads, what happens to the running mates and how supporters are transferred between parties. There is also no guarantee that voters will follow elite instructions. An Atiku endorsement of Obi would not automatically deliver Atiku’s northern vote. An Obi endorsement of Atiku would not automatically transfer younger urban voters or the South-East. Nigerian politicians often mistake negotiations among leaders for consolidation among electorates. The opposition nevertheless understands the arithmetic. Tinubu won in 2023 with 36.61 per cent of the valid votes; 8.79 million votes. Atiku and Obi together received more than 13 million. That does not mean a joint ticket would have automatically defeated Tinubu, because elections are shaped by turnout, geography and the constitutional requirement for national spread. But it shows why fragmentation remains the APC’s quiet ally. Unless the coalition produces a credible agreement quickly, it risks becoming a committee for managing defeat. The register question The emphasis on 103.43 million voters has also reopened an important transparency dispute. INEC says the total follows the addition of approximately 10.77 million new registrants. Atiku has demanded that the preliminary register be made available for public inspection, alleging that an online page intended for that purpose was empty. The allegation does not establish manipulation. Technical delays or publication problems are not evidence of a compromised register. But INEC should resolve the issue immediately. A national figure cannot substitute for a register that citizens and parties can scrutinise. The public must be able to identify duplicate entries, deceased persons, omissions and questionable registrations before the final roll is certified. If parties are already building campaign strategies around precise regional totals, voters deserve access to the underlying data. First, watch the language and attendance at Saturday’s Kaduna rally. A large gathering will demonstrate organisational capacity, but the more important question is whether influential northern leaders offer genuine commitments or merely perform ceremonial loyalty. Second, watch whether the 90-day economic plan produces identifiable benefits before election day. Its political credibility will depend on outcomes, not intentions. Third, watch the opposition negotiations. A consensus announced after ballots and campaign loyalties have hardened may be largely symbolic. Finally, watch INEC. Publication and scrutiny of the voter register will be an early test of whether the Commission intends to manage doubts proactively or react only after they become political crises. Tinubu enters the northern campaign with the strongest political machine, an expanding network of governors and a divided opposition. Those advantages are substantial. But the North’s 56 million registrations are not a blank cheque. Its voters are living with insecurity, expensive food, high transport costs and the uneven consequences of economic reform. The APC is campaigning on structure and patience. The opposition is campaigning on hardship and change, but without yet agreeing on whose change.
